BBC News. LD datePublished Wed 14 Oct 21:17 BST; dateModified Thu 15 Oct 05:30 BST (DIFFERS - report both). By Tiffany Wertheimer.
LD headline: 'Starlink: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds'. Front-page headline drops the 'Starlink:' prefix - BBC re-headlined without republishing.
Musk on X: Starshield, the military-grade sister service to Starlink, is controlled by the US government and 'any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately [the US president]'. Full post: 'Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS.'
Musk added Starlink is for 'civilian or defensive activities and cannot be used for offensive military action, as doing so would be inappropriate for a commercial company'.
CONTEXT OF THE POST: Musk was replying to Ukraine's former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who had said connectivity was partially restored by Wednesday evening and wrote on X: 'Removing Starshield's speed limit entirely is now critical for Ukraine's defense', thanking Musk and asking for his 'continued support'. Musk replied about an hour later.
SOFTER ZELENSKY QUOTE - CONFLICTS IN TONE WITH THE GUARDIAN'S PIERS MORGAN QUOTE. Zelensky told UK media: 'I hope that it's a mistake, maybe [a] huge technical problem. I don't know, but we are asking to... switch [it] on.'
MECHANISM: Starlink restricted speed limits on Tuesday night to 100mph (160km/h); any weapons travelling faster lost connectivity.
Beskrestnov (Zelensky's adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov), on Telegram Wednesday morning: 'It is clear that this action cannot be a coincidence and is related to the current political situation.'
MUSK ON ZELENSKY: late Wednesday on X, replying to a post saying Zelensky would not end the war until Russia was defeated, Musk wrote: 'And so the slaughter continues ... Time for Zelensky to go.' Earlier this week Musk said: 'I agree, time for Ukraine to get a new leader', after Trump said it was 'time for Ukraine to get a new president'.
Zelensky has said the US threatened to restrict intelligence sharing if he did not sign up to Trump's energy ceasefire; Trump denied this on Tuesday.
OVERNIGHT FRESH: in the early hours of Thursday, Russian strikes killed two people in the Dnipropetrovsk region, regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha said.
At least 600,000 people across Ukraine left without electricity; residents said they received no warning of incoming drones. Zelensky called it 'one of the largest attacks'; 'a significant part of the drones were shot down' but there were 'also hits'.
Diesel deal figure: US made a deal with Russia to import 300,000 tonnes of its diesel.
Ukraine under martial law since the 2022 invasion, so elections are suspended.
